spec_match.rationale: Targets the maxwritewithoutresponsesizechanged half of the feature with a clear cached-vs-listening comparison, and the code-path panel shows the real listener plus the per-write read pattern; the simulation is explicit about being simulated and about the platform-dependent reject-vs-truncate behaviour it models.

interactive.rationale: Run animates both lanes against a shared link, a Force-renegotiation button lets the user trigger the drop early, Reset restores everything, and per-lane writing-size/delivered/truncated counters plus a timestamped log narrate the divergence.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises the listener, the re-chunk, and the silent-truncation bug you get without them — the page delivers exactly that comparison.

edge_cases.rationale: Renegotiation is guarded against firing twice, forcing it after completion is a no-op, re-running mid-run resets cleanly, the log is capped, and the lost-bytes arithmetic in the verdict is consistent with the truncation model.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5177569273053184 alongside the sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The suite's gatt-server-is-an-event-target assertion is exactly the contract this page's listener depends on, and the 1 pass / 7 fail run here is honest for a build with no navigator.bluetooth; partial carries the vacuous user-gesture-assertion flag recorded on the mtu-probe critique.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): load behaviour observed — reset() painted both lanes idle at 182 B with zeroed counters, console clean ('[ble-mtu:change] ready') — and both screenshots show the full two-lane layout; the run/force/reset flow is click-driven and judged from wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert fires renegotiation-fired with before/after sizes and comparison-complete with both lanes' truncation counts; console is clean at load.

design_system.rationale: Layout, buttons and log colours follow the design system (rose ~4.8:1 and accent-blue ~7:1 on stone both pass), but the 'Listening for the change' lane heading uses --accent-emerald on stone (~3.7:1), the recurring shared-palette AA shortfall.

accessibility.rationale: The event log is an aria-live=polite list with an aria-label, the verdict lands in an aria-live output, lane headings pair aria-hidden icons with text, counters are definition lists, and all controls are real buttons with disabled-state management.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px and 1280px: lanes stack, counters wrap to a single column, the long event name wraps inside the note, and there is no horizontal overflow or clipped control on either class.

openQuestions.title: Progress tracks lack accessible names
openQuestions.detail: The two .track progress bars are purely visual divs with a percentage rendered inside a <b>; unlike the sibling transfer-simulator they carry no role or label at all. Giving each a role=progressbar (or role=img with a label referencing the lane heading) plus aria-valuenow, or simply relying on the existing text while marking the track aria-hidden, would make the state of each lane unambiguous to a screen reader during a run.

openQuestions.title: Consider wiring the real event when hardware is present
openQuestions.detail: The page is a simulation by design, but on a Chrome 157+ build with a paired device (via the mtu-probe flow) the real maxwritewithoutresponsesizechanged event could drive the same two-lane visual, turning the simulation into live evidence when circumstances allow and falling back to the simulation otherwise. Additive enhancement, not a defect — the honest simulated framing is already correct.

summary: The edge-case concept done right: cached-size-vs-listener is exactly the bug class the change event exists to prevent, the silent-truncation model matches the failure mode the page's own copy documents as the dangerous one, and the force-renegotiation control makes the race tangible. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v157/web-bluetooth-bluetoothremotegattserver-maxwritewithoutresponsesize/size-change-event/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots of the initialised two-lane state, clean console; feature /conformance/ route 1 pass / 7 fail, honest for this build with no navigator.bluetooth — the simulation intentionally requires none). The run flow is click-driven and judged from wiring, which guards double-renegotiation and mid-run resets correctly. Remaining polish: accessible names for the progress tracks and the shared emerald-on-stone contrast shortfall on the lane heading.
